q: After a workstation compromise, an attacker moved freely to servers across the same flat internal network. Which architectural change BEST limits this lateral movement in the future?
c: Deploying a stronger firewall at the Internet edge
Enforcing longer passwords on all workstations
Segmenting the network and restricting traffic between zones
Increasing logging on the core switches

q: In a three-tier web application exposed to the Internet, where should the database server be positioned?
c: In an internal zone reachable only from the application tier
In the DMZ alongside the public web servers
On the public subnet behind a host firewall
On the same VLAN as user workstations

q: Users on an office VLAN intermittently receive network settings from an unauthorized device, which routes their traffic through an attacker-controlled gateway. Which switch feature MOST directly prevents this?
c: Port security limiting MAC addresses per port
DHCP snooping with trusted ports
Spanning Tree Protocol root guard
802.1X port-based network access control

q: Two branch offices must protect all traffic exchanged between their networks across the Internet, including concealing the original internal IP headers. Which configuration meets this requirement?
c: IPsec ESP in transport mode between the gateways
IPsec AH in tunnel mode between the sites
TLS on each application crossing the link
IPsec ESP in tunnel mode between the site gateways

q: Remote employees reach corporate systems through a VPN, while their other web traffic bypasses the tunnel and goes straight to the Internet. What is the PRIMARY security concern with this split-tunnel arrangement?
c: Encryption strength drops when the tunnel is split
Split tunnels consume extra VPN bandwidth
The device can bridge Internet threats into the corporate network
Users lose access to internal resources

q: A utility connects its plant control network to the corporate IT network for production reporting, but engineering workstations must never be directly reachable from the business side. Which design BEST enforces this?
c: A brokered intermediary zone that terminates all cross-boundary flows
Separate VLANs for IT and OT on the shared core switches
Host-based firewalls on each engineering workstation
Encryption of all traffic passing between IT and OT

q: A security analyst discovers that an attacker on a user-facing access port sent traffic into a restricted VLAN by crafting frames with two 802.1Q tags. Which switch configuration change BEST prevents this double-tagging attack?
c: Enable dynamic trunking negotiation on all access ports so the switch controls trunk formation
Assign the native VLAN on trunk links to an unused VLAN ID and hard-code user ports as access ports
Configure DHCP snooping so untrusted ports cannot deliver tagged frames into the network
Apply port mirroring to copy access-port traffic to a monitoring VLAN for inspection

q: A hospital wants to ensure that only managed, corporate-owned devices can connect to wired network ports in public waiting areas, where visitors can physically reach the jacks. Which control BEST meets this requirement?
c: MAC address filtering maintained on each access switch
Placing all waiting-area ports in a guest VLAN with Internet-only access
802.1X port-based authentication using certificates issued to corporate devices
Physically locking network jacks and disabling all unused wall ports

q: A small office currently uses WPA2-Personal with a shared passphrase on its wireless network. The owner asks what security benefit an upgrade to WPA3-Personal would provide. Which improvement is MOST significant?
c: Simultaneous Authentication of Equals resists offline dictionary attacks against captured handshakes
It replaces the shared passphrase with per-user credentials tied to a RADIUS server
It introduces AES encryption, which WPA2 did not support
It hides the SSID so attackers can no longer discover the network name

q: An external scan shows a customer-facing payment portal still accepts TLS 1.0 connections for legacy browser compatibility, though analytics show fewer than 0.1 percent of clients use it. As security manager, what should you recommend FIRST?
c: Deploy a web application firewall rule to inspect TLS 1.0 sessions for attack signatures
Disable TLS 1.0 and 1.1 on the portal after a short notice period to the residual client base
Direct the application team to migrate every internal service to TLS 1.3 simultaneously
Accept the risk formally, since fewer than 0.1 percent of connections are affected

q: A SaaS provider's traffic was briefly routed through an unrelated foreign network after another autonomous system announced a more specific BGP prefix covering the provider's address space. Which measure BEST reduces the chance of a recurrence?
c: Enable MD5 authentication on all BGP peering sessions with adjacent providers
Require TLS for all customer connections so intercepted traffic remains unreadable
Publish route origin authorizations for its prefixes and use transit providers that drop RPKI-invalid announcements
Advertise more specific prefixes continuously so competing announcements never win best-path selection

q: After a DNS cache-poisoning incident redirected employees to a counterfeit payroll portal, an architect proposes deploying DNSSEC validation on the enterprise resolvers. Which outcome should management expect this control to deliver?
c: Queries and responses will be encrypted, hiding employees' lookups from eavesdroppers
Known-malicious domains will be blocked through signed reputation feeds
Zone transfers will require mutually authenticated TLS sessions between servers
Resolvers will be able to verify that answers are authentic and unmodified via digital signatures

q: A company adopting zero trust currently grants full intranet access to any device that connects through the campus LAN or the VPN. Which core principle should the new architecture apply in place of this assumption?
c: Access decisions must be made per session based on identity, device posture, and context rather than network location
All internal traffic must be blocked until the perimeter firewall is replaced with a next-generation model
Users on the corporate LAN may retain implicit trust while only VPN users are continuously re-authenticated
Encrypting all internal traffic between endpoints is sufficient to establish trust

q: A team configured an IPsec VPN to a partner using Authentication Header, but the tunnel fails whenever traffic passes through the branch office's NAT gateway. The partner also requires confidentiality for the data. What should the team do?
c: Replace the NAT gateway with static one-to-one address mappings so AH integrity checks remain valid
Switch AH from tunnel mode to transport mode so the outer header is no longer protected
Use ESP with NAT traversal, which provides integrity and confidentiality and tolerates address translation
Encapsulate the AH tunnel inside GRE so the translated header is hidden from the integrity check

q: A retailer is replacing its MPLS circuits with SD-WAN that sends branch traffic over local broadband Internet links, including direct breakout to cloud applications. Which consideration is MOST important for the security architecture?
c: Preserving MPLS-equivalent quality of service so voice and video traffic does not degrade
Ensuring branch routers have capacity to carry full Internet BGP routing tables
Consolidating branch firewalls into the SD-WAN controller, which now centrally enforces all policy
Protecting traffic that now rides the public Internet with authenticated encrypted tunnels and inspection at cloud breakout points

q: Finance staff keep receiving convincing invoice emails that spoof the company's own domain in the visible From header. SPF is already published. Which addition BEST enables receiving servers to reject these forged messages?
c: Publish a DMARC reject policy with DKIM signing so receivers verify alignment with the visible From domain
Tighten the SPF record to a hard-fail qualifier so unauthorized sending hosts are refused
Deploy S/MIME certificates to all finance employees so their outbound mail is digitally signed
Enable opportunistic TLS between mail gateways to stop interception of messages in transit

q: A company deploying VoIP wants to keep the audio content of calls confidential as it crosses the office network. Which protocol is specifically designed to provide this protection?
c: SIP over TLS
RTP
SRTP

q: An HVAC vendor needs recurring remote access to maintenance servers on the facilities network. Today a technician connects through a shared desktop-sharing tool installed on an engineer's workstation. Which redesign BEST manages this third-party connectivity?
c: Issue the vendor a standard employee VPN profile so sessions traverse the corporate remote access concentrator
Route vendor sessions through a dedicated jump host with MFA, individual accounts, session recording, and access scoped to the maintenance servers
Keep the desktop-sharing tool but restrict its use to business hours through firewall schedules
Require the vendor to sign a connection agreement documenting their security obligations and liability

q: An online brokerage's 10 Gbps Internet links were saturated for hours by a 300 Gbps reflection flood; on-premises appliances never saw manageable load. Management asks how to withstand a repeat event. Which approach is MOST effective?
c: Upgrade the perimeter firewalls to higher-throughput models with SYN flood protection features
Implement rate limiting and geographic blocking ACLs on the enterprise border routers
Increase Internet capacity to 40 Gbps spread across redundant carriers and diverse paths
Engage an upstream cloud scrubbing or CDN-based mitigation service that filters attack traffic before it reaches the enterprise links

q: During an incident investigation, analysts find timestamps across firewalls, servers, and domain controllers differ by minutes, and one syslog source is hours off, making event correlation unreliable. Which design change BEST prevents this problem?
c: Configure each device to poll any public NTP pool server of its administrator's choosing
Synchronize device clocks manually during quarterly maintenance windows
Deploy a redundant internal time hierarchy traceable to trusted references, with authenticated NTP required for all logging devices
Compensate in the SIEM by applying a per-source clock offset to timestamps as events are ingested

q: A firewall protecting a cardholder-data enclave suffers a software crash. By design, no traffic may pass while the device is down, even though this interrupts business transactions until service is restored. Which principle does this design illustrate?
c: Fail secure (fail closed)
Fail open
Graceful degradation
High availability

q: An internal HR web application must become reachable to employees on the Internet without exposing the application server directly. The architect wants external connections terminated in a controlled zone, with inspection and authentication applied before requests reach the internal server. Which component fits this design?
c: A forward proxy configured in employees' browser settings
A NAT rule on the perimeter firewall publishing the server's internal address
A site-to-site VPN concentrator linking employees' home networks to the datacenter
A reverse proxy in a screened subnet that relays validated requests to the internal application

q: Penetration testers stood up a rogue access point broadcasting the corporate SSID and harvested employees' 802.1X credentials when laptops attempted to authenticate through it. Which control BEST prevents corporate devices from disclosing credentials to such an evil twin?
c: Configure supplicants to validate the RADIUS server certificate against a pinned trusted CA and refuse authentication otherwise
Reduce access point transmit power so the corporate wireless signal does not extend beyond the building
Enforce a longer and more complex password policy for all wireless network users
Enable MAC address filtering so only corporate laptops can associate with the wireless network

q: Monitoring alerts that a switch's MAC address table filled with tens of thousands of entries learned from one access port, and the switch began flooding unicast frames out all ports, letting a connected host capture other users' traffic. Which control directly counters this attack?
c: Storm control thresholds for broadcast and multicast traffic volumes
Port security limiting the number of source MAC addresses learned per port
BPDU guard to shut down ports that receive spanning tree protocol messages
Dynamic ARP inspection validating address resolution messages on untrusted ports

q: A network engineer proposes that switch, router, and firewall administration interfaces be reachable only from a physically separate management network rather than from the production LAN. What is the PRIMARY security benefit of this design?
c: It increases throughput by removing management traffic from busy production links
It lets administrators manage devices conveniently from any workstation in the enterprise
A compromised production host cannot reach device management planes, and administration remains possible during production network incidents
It eliminates the need for authentication on device interfaces since the management network is isolated

q: Two internal microservices exchange sensitive account data across the datacenter network. Policy requires that each service verify the identity of the other before any data flows, in addition to encrypting the session. Which mechanism satisfies both requirements?
c: TLS with server certificates issued by the internal certificate authority
Mutual TLS in which each service presents and validates a certificate during the handshake
IP allowlists restricting which datacenter hosts may open connections to each service
Hashing each payload with SHA-256 before it is transmitted between the services

q: A company carries iSCSI storage traffic across the same converged datacenter network as ordinary server VLANs to reduce cabling costs. An auditor flags the design as exposing block storage to any compromised server. Which combination of measures BEST addresses the risk?
c: Enable jumbo frames and QoS tagging so storage traffic receives priority over user traffic
Isolate storage traffic on dedicated non-routed VLANs or a separate fabric, and require mutual CHAP authentication between initiators and targets
Replace iSCSI with Fibre Channel, since a dedicated FC fabric is immune to network-based attacks
Encrypt data at rest on the storage arrays so intercepted LUN traffic is unreadable to attackers

q: An IPv4-only enterprise discovers workstations exfiltrating data through tunnels established after receiving rogue IPv6 router advertisements on the LAN, bypassing egress controls that inspect only IPv4. Which action BEST remediates this exposure?
c: Block protocol 41 encapsulation at the Internet perimeter so IPv6 packets cannot leave inside IPv4
Rely on the existing NAT boundary, since private internal addressing prevents hosts from reaching external tunnel endpoints
Enable RA Guard on access ports and bring IPv6 within egress policy and monitoring, disabling it where it is not needed
Deploy intrusion detection signatures that alert on traffic patterns of known IPv6 tunneling utilities

q: A SOC relies on internal DNS resolver logs to detect malware command-and-control domains. Detections are dropping because many endpoints and browsers now resolve names via encrypted DNS over HTTPS directly to public providers. What should the security team do FIRST?
c: Decrypt all outbound HTTPS at the forward proxy so encrypted DNS queries become visible again
Accept encrypted DNS as a privacy improvement and retire the DNS-based detection content
Migrate detection to flow-record analysis, which does not depend on observing name resolution
Use endpoint and browser policy to direct managed devices to the enterprise resolver and block known external DoH services at egress

q: A board meeting held on the company's video conferencing platform was joined by an uninvited participant who obtained the reusable meeting link from a forwarded email. Which combination of platform controls BEST prevents a recurrence for sensitive meetings?
c: Unique per-meeting links with authenticated join, waiting-room admission, and locking the session once attendees arrive
End-to-end encryption so the meeting's audio and video streams cannot be read in transit
Recording every sensitive session so any intrusion can be identified and reviewed afterward
A published policy stating that links for sensitive meetings must never be forwarded

q: Two campus buildings are connected by a provider-delivered metro Ethernet circuit operating at layer 2. Security requires line-rate encryption of all traffic between the buildings, including non-IP protocols, with minimal added latency. Which technology BEST fits?
c: Site-to-site IPsec tunnels between routers placed at each building
MACsec (IEEE 802.1AE) enabled on the switch interfaces facing the metro Ethernet link
TLS enforced for every application communicating across the inter-building link
PPTP tunnels established between the campus core switches at each site

q: During an architecture review, a network engineer argues that a branch office does not need a firewall because all hosts use RFC 1918 private addresses behind NAT, so outsiders cannot reach them anyway. What is the BEST response from the security architect?
c: Agree, because NAT hides internal addresses and drops unsolicited inbound packets by design
Require proxy ARP on the edge router to conceal internal MAC addresses from the Internet
Explain that NAT is an address translation mechanism, not a security control, and require a firewall enforcing explicit policy
Replace NAT with IPv6 global addressing so IPsec can be used end to end without translation

q: An audit finds that administrators manage core switches over Telnet from their desktops, so device credentials cross the network in cleartext. Which remediation should the security team recommend FIRST?
c: Replace Telnet with SSH for all device management sessions
Enable SNMPv3 on the switches for configuration changes
Require administrators to change device passwords after every session
Move the switches to a separate VLAN so users cannot reach them

q: A legal team must email highly sensitive case files to outside counsel. The email gateway already negotiates opportunistic TLS with most partner domains. Why might the security officer still require S/MIME encryption for these messages?
c: TLS cannot encrypt attachments larger than the negotiated record size
TLS protects mail only between servers, while S/MIME keeps content encrypted end to end, including on relays and in mailboxes
S/MIME provides faster delivery because encrypted messages bypass content inspection at every relaying gateway
Opportunistic TLS always downgrades to cleartext when either mail server also supports S/MIME

q: Penetration testers repeatedly exploit SQL injection in a public web application over HTTPS. Code fixes will take months to ship. Which network control BEST reduces this exposure in the meantime?
c: A stateful packet-filtering firewall restricting inbound traffic to TCP port 443
A network intrusion prevention system watching the encrypted sessions inline
A screened subnet separating the web tier from the database tier
A web application firewall terminating TLS and filtering application-layer requests

q: Your company acquires a smaller firm, and executives want the two office networks fully joined within a week to speed integration. The acquired network's security posture is unknown. What should the security architect recommend FIRST?
c: Connect the networks only through a restrictive, monitored interconnect while the acquired environment is assessed
Merge the networks immediately and schedule a vulnerability scan of the acquired hosts for the following quarter
Extend the corporate zero trust policy engine across the acquired firm before allowing any connectivity
Require the acquired firm to re-address its network into the corporate IP plan before any traffic is exchanged

q: A security team notices its IDS misses sessions during peak hours. The sensor receives traffic from a switch SPAN port that is frequently oversubscribed. What is the BEST way to give the sensor complete visibility?
c: Configure an additional SPAN session on the same switch to share the mirroring load
Deploy a dedicated network TAP on the monitored link and feed the sensor from it
Move the sensor inline so the switch must forward every packet through it
Enable NetFlow export so the sensor can reconstruct the missing sessions

q: A hotel wants guests to join Wi-Fi without accounts or passwords, but a review found the current open SSID lets anyone eavesdrop on guest traffic. Which option BEST addresses the eavesdropping while preserving the frictionless join experience?
c: Publish a shared WPA2-Personal passphrase on lobby signage so every guest device can encrypt its traffic
Add a captive portal so guests must accept terms before their traffic is allowed to flow
Enable Wi-Fi Enhanced Open (OWE) so each guest session is individually encrypted without authentication
Hide the SSID so only guests who are told the network name can associate

q: A configuration review shows routers and switches answer SNMP read and write requests using the community string 'private' from any source address. Which remediation BEST addresses the risk?
c: Change the community string to a long random value stored in the password vault
Disable SNMP entirely and rely on syslog for all device monitoring needs
Restrict SNMP to the management VLAN while keeping version 2c for tool compatibility
Migrate to SNMPv3 with authentication and privacy, and restrict sources to management hosts

q: An external assessment reveals that the company's Internet-facing DNS server answers queries for internal hostnames, exposing the names and addresses of domain controllers and file servers. Which design change BEST corrects this?
c: Implement split DNS so external servers host only public records and internal zones stay on internal resolvers
Sign all zones with DNSSEC so external parties cannot read the internal records
Block TCP port 53 at the firewall so only small UDP queries reach the server
Rename internal hosts with unpredictable labels so leaked records reveal nothing useful

q: Threat intelligence indicates an adversary is recording the company's encrypted VPN traffic for later analysis, and the concentrator's private key could plausibly be stolen in the future. Which property MOST directly limits the damage from that scenario?
c: Longer RSA keys on the concentrator certificate to make factoring computationally infeasible
Forward secrecy from ephemeral key agreement, so past sessions cannot be decrypted with the stolen key
Certificate pinning on clients so a stolen key cannot be used to impersonate the gateway
Rotating the concentrator certificate quarterly so any stolen key ages out quickly

q: A manufacturer is cabling a new production floor filled with large motors and welding equipment. Data errors from electrical interference are a major concern, and cable runs pass through areas open to visiting contractors. Which transmission medium BEST fits these conditions?
c: Shielded twisted pair, because grounding the shield eliminates all induced noise
Coaxial cable, because its solid core resists vibration from heavy machinery
Fiber optic cable, because it is immune to electromagnetic interference and difficult to tap unnoticed
Unshielded twisted pair at a higher category rating, because faster cable rejects interference

q: A hospital's 802.1X deployment cannot cover infusion pumps and badge printers that lack supplicant support, so those switch ports use MAC Authentication Bypass. The CISO asks how the risk MAB introduces should be handled. What is the BEST response?
c: MAB is equivalent to certificate authentication because the RADIUS server validates each MAC address
Disable MAB and leave those ports unauthenticated since the devices are trusted medical equipment
Replace every non-supplicant device immediately regardless of clinical replacement cycles
Keep MAB but place those devices in tightly restricted VLANs with ACLs and monitor for MAC spoofing

q: A company plans to deploy TLS interception on its web proxy to inspect outbound traffic for data loss and malware. The privacy officer raises concerns about employees' personal banking and health sites. What is the BEST way to proceed?
c: Inspect by default but bypass decryption for defined categories such as financial and health sites, and disclose the practice to employees
Inspect all traffic uniformly because selective bypass would create blind spots attackers could exploit
Abandon interception and rely on DNS-based filtering so employee content is never decrypted
Inspect all traffic but retain decrypted content for only thirty days to limit privacy exposure

q: Twice this month the network went down after employees plugged unmanaged desktop switches into wall jacks, triggering spanning tree recalculations and a bridging loop. Which control BEST prevents a recurrence at the access layer?
c: Increase the core switches' spanning tree priority so they always remain the root bridge
Enable BPDU Guard on access ports so any port receiving bridge protocol messages is shut down
Enable port security so ports that learn more than one MAC address are disabled
Deploy DHCP snooping so devices behind rogue switches cannot obtain addresses

q: An enterprise is moving its data center to a software-defined network in which a central controller programs all switching behavior through southbound APIs. During threat modeling, which risk should receive the HIGHEST priority?
c: Loss of a single leaf switch, because SDN cannot reroute around failed hardware
Encrypted east-west traffic, because inspection tools cannot read flows between virtual machines
Compromise of the controller or its APIs, because it would grant an attacker authority over the entire network's forwarding behavior
Vendor lock-in from proprietary northbound applications, because migration costs would rise

q: An office of 300 staff uses one WPA2-Personal passphrase for the corporate SSID. After several departures the passphrase has never changed, because updating every device is disruptive. Which change BEST resolves the underlying problem?
c: Adopt a longer passphrase and rotate it every ninety days through the MDM platform
Move the corporate network to a hidden SSID so former employees cannot find it
Enable MAC address filtering so only inventoried corporate devices can associate
Migrate to WPA2/WPA3-Enterprise so each user authenticates individually and access ends when accounts are disabled

q: During an external scan, testers download the company's entire DNS zone using an AXFR request against the authoritative name server, revealing every registered host. What is the BEST corrective action?
c: Restrict zone transfers to the specific addresses of authorized secondary name servers
Disable recursion on the authoritative server so it answers only for its own zones
Shorten the zone's TTL values so any leaked records expire quickly
Place the name server behind a load balancer so AXFR sessions cannot complete

q: A defense contractor sends sensitive traffic between two sites over a carrier service advertised as fully encrypted. The security architect learns each carrier node decrypts and re-encrypts traffic as it forwards it. What is the MOST appropriate conclusion?
c: The design is acceptable because traffic is never exposed on any physical wire between nodes
Link encryption leaves plaintext exposed inside intermediate nodes, so the contractor should add end-to-end encryption it controls
The carrier should be asked to add a second layer of link encryption at each hop for defense in depth
The design fails only if the carrier's nodes are located outside the contractor's home country

q: A hospital plans to deploy an inline IPS on the network segment carrying real-time patient telemetry. Engineers must choose the appliance's behavior if it loses power or crashes. Which configuration BEST reflects sound risk management?
c: Fail closed, because blocking all traffic during a failure prevents any attack from passing uninspected
Fail closed, but issue clinicians a procedure to physically re-cable around the appliance during outages
Fail open with a hardware bypass, because interrupting patient telemetry poses a greater risk than briefly uninspected traffic
Fail open permanently by running the sensor in passive SPAN mode so it can never affect traffic

q: An ISP notifies a company that packets bearing other organizations' source addresses are leaving its network as part of a reflection DDoS campaign. Which control at the Internet edge BEST prevents the company's network from being misused this way?
c: Inbound rate limiting on the border router to blunt reflected replies arriving from the campaign
Blackhole routing that discards all traffic destined for the DDoS victims' address ranges
RPKI route origin validation so forged BGP announcements are rejected at the border
Egress filtering that drops outbound packets whose source addresses are not from the company's assigned ranges

q: A quarterly review finds a firewall rule permitting any source to any destination on all ports, added during a troubleshooting session eight months earlier and forgotten. What does this finding MOST clearly indicate is missing?
c: A change management process with expiration and periodic recertification of firewall rules
A next-generation firewall, since legacy platforms cannot express granular policies
An intrusion prevention system to compensate for the overly permissive rule
Separation of duties so firewall administrators cannot approve their own emergency changes

q: Facilities installs a point-to-point wireless bridge to link two office buildings across a public street, replacing a leased line. What additional safeguard is MOST important before carrying corporate traffic over the bridge?
c: Narrow-beam directional antennas so the signal cannot be received away from the path
Strong encryption of all traffic crossing the bridge, since the radio signal extends beyond company control
MAC address filtering so only the two bridge radios can associate with each other
Reduced transmit power so the link cannot be detected from street level

q: Security policy forbids unauthorized wireless access points, but a walkthrough discovered an employee-installed AP wired into a conference room jack. Management wants continuous detection rather than periodic walkthroughs. Which control BEST meets that goal?
c: Quarterly wireless penetration tests covering every office location
A NAC agent on corporate laptops that reports nearby SSIDs to a central console
A wireless intrusion prevention system with sensors that continuously scan for rogue devices
An annual review of switch CAM tables for unrecognized MAC addresses

q: Weeks after moving to SIP trunking, a company receives a massive bill for international calls placed overnight through its IP-PBX. Investigation finds Internet-exposed SIP registration protected only by weak extension passwords. Which combination MOST effectively prevents recurrence?
c: Enable SRTP on all calls so attackers cannot listen to the fraudulent conversations
Move the PBX behind NAT so external endpoints can no longer send packets to it
Publish the trunk on a nonstandard port so scanners stop finding the registration service
Restrict signaling to the provider's addresses, enforce strong authentication over TLS, and set toll restrictions with alerts

q: A retailer offloads its storefront to a CDN that terminates TLS at global edge nodes. An architect discovers the CDN fetches content from the origin data center over plain HTTP because that connection is considered trusted. What is the MOST significant issue?
c: Customers' browsers will display certificate warnings because the edge certificate does not match the origin
CDN caching will serve stale pages because HTTP responses cannot carry cache-control headers
Traffic between the CDN edge and the origin crosses the Internet unencrypted, exposing sessions and data despite the padlock users see
TLS termination at the edge violates PCI DSS, which requires encryption to terminate only inside the cardholder environment
